blind_spot_pass: Opposite-direction visual/voluntary-breathing findings, task modality, outcome mismatch, continuous respiratory angle and stimulus/response time-lag differences were checked. Follow-up separates external multisensory synchrony judgments from interoceptive and physiological synchrony, and checks RT-judgment dissociations, cross-modal transfer and non-respiratory rhythms. No claim of universal direction or direct replication is supported.
synchrony_search_conclusion: No directly matching external audio-tactile or audio-visual inhale-versus-exhale synchrony-judgment study identified in this targeted search. This is not a claim of absence from the literature. Released tactile-target RTs do not measure subjective simultaneity, binding-window width or synchrony sensitivity.

sources.title: Dissociation of perception and action in audiovisual multisensory integration
sources.access: Full primary paper; experiments and judgment results inspected
sources.finding: RT/race-model integration and simultaneity/order judgments had different timing requirements; judgment experiment n=6
sources.transfer_limit: No respiratory comparison; small experiment; cannot convert a raw RT shift into subjective simultaneity or binding-window width

sources.title: Left Motor delta Oscillations Reflect Asynchrony Detection in Multisensory Speech Perception
sources.access: Full primary paper; procedure and behavioral results inspected
sources.role: explicit audiovisual synchrony detection and RT
sources.finding: N=23; synchronous versus 400 ms delayed speech; face masking impaired sensitivity and slowed RT; asynchrony main effect on RT p=.42
sources.transfer_limit: No breathing-phase factor; no response deadline; speech differs from tactile-target speeded detection

sources.title: The development of audio-visual temporal precision precedes its rapid recalibration
sources.access: Full primary paper; abstract and task methods inspected
sources.role: audio-tactile, audiovisual and visuotactile simultaneity task reference
sources.finding: Reanalysis of developmental datasets showed modality differences in temporal precision and rapid recalibration
sources.transfer_limit: No respiratory-phase comparison; audiovisual findings do not automatically transfer to touch

sources.title: The rhythm of sensory input shapes audio-visual temporal processing
sources.access: Primary abstract and figure descriptions opened; publisher inaccessible and PMC browser challenge
sources.role: external stimulus rhythm and audiovisual temporal binding windows
sources.finding: Higher stimulation frequency narrowed temporal binding windows; speech-like streams widened them
sources.transfer_limit: External stimulus rhythm is not respiration; not a full-paper audit or evidence of an inhale/exhale direction

sources.title: Perception of audio-visual synchrony is modulated by walking speed and step-cycle phase
sources.access: Publisher full text; abstract, participants, timing verification and procedure inspected
sources.role: bodily rhythm and explicit external synchrony judgments
sources.finding: N=21; slow walking widened synchrony window and increased RT; judgments also varied with step-cycle phase
sources.transfer_limit: Walking rather than respiration; body-rhythm analogy does not predict an inhale/exhale effect

sources.title: Influences of Respiratory Cycle on Simple Reaction Time
sources.access: Publisher abstract opened; full text restricted
sources.finding: Both reported experiments found faster responses with expiration
sources.transfer_limit: Different stimulus modality and respiratory manipulations; sample details not reconstructed from inaccessible full text

sources.title: Response speed is modulated by respiratory phase
sources.access: Institutional research report opened; journal full text returned 403; author laboratory publication page returned 502
sources.finding: Institution reports N=35, monitored nasal airflow, visual psychomotor vigilance task, approximately 41 ms faster exhalation than inhalation
sources.transfer_limit: Not a full-paper audit; different modality/task and monitored physiology; do not interpret as a matched estimand or claim magnitude replication

sources.title: Respiration Facilitates Behavior During Multisensory Integration
sources.access: Publisher full text; methods/results/respiratory phase definition inspected
sources.role: closest multisensory task context; subphase caveat
sources.finding: N=40; measured respiration; faster around peak inspiration/early expiration, slower at expiration-to-inspiration transition
sources.transfer_limit: Continuous/subphase analysis and race-model integration are not binary phase labels, baseline subtraction or PPS boundaries

sources.title: Respiration, Heartbeat, and Conscious Tactile Perception
sources.access: Primary abstract and figure descriptions opened; publisher/PMC full text challenged or blocked
sources.finding: N=41; near-threshold tactile detection highest shortly after expiration onset
sources.transfer_limit: Detection rate rather than reaction time; not a latency replication

sources.title: Inhalation boosts perceptual awareness and decision speed
sources.access: Primary abstract and institutional record opened; publisher full text blocked; institutional download was a one-page abstract record
sources.finding: N=30; near-threshold visual orientation decisions faster during inhalation
sources.transfer_limit: Different decision task; rules out a universal claim, not a direct statistical contradiction between matched estimands

sources.title: The influence of the respiratory cycle on reaction times in sensory-cognitive paradigms
sources.access: Publisher full text; respiratory coding, task methods/results and timing analyses inspected
sources.finding: RT covaries with respiration across multiple sensory-cognitive tasks; stimulus/response alignment matters
sources.transfer_limit: Measured respiratory state plus subphase is not the released scheduled/instructed binary label

sources.title: Respiration shapes response speed and accuracy with a systematic time lag
sources.access: Primary abstract/figure descriptions opened; indexed full-text excerpts inspected; PMC full-text access intermittent
sources.finding: Across 12 datasets, RT association strongest for respiration about 2 seconds before response
sources.transfer_limit: Does not establish a universal binary exhale advantage; analysis cannot be reproduced with missing respiratory waveforms
